quandoUsar: A fixed moment people are waiting for, such as a launch, a live event, or a registration deadline, with large digits in the center of a section (`variant="large"`).
A deadline inside a banner, card, or table cell, on a single line (`variant="compact"`).
Screens that must change on their own at zero: the digits become `completeLabel` (default “Live now”) and `onComplete` fires once, immediately, even with the tab hidden.
quandoEvitar: It does not suit elapsed time, such as a stopwatch counting up: it only counts down to `target`.
Use `announcement-bar` when the deadline accompanies a message at the top of the site; it has its own countdown inside the message.
Use `slot-text` or `animated-counter` for numbers that change by event, such as a price or total, with no clock behind them.
acessibilidade: The root is `role="timer"` named by `label` (default “Time remaining”); the animated digits are hidden and a hidden text states the time in full, without seconds while more than a minute remains.
`role="timer"` does not announce changes; if the end matters to screen reader users, announce it in your own live region from `onComplete`.
The unit names, both visible and read aloud (“Days”, “3 days, 4 hours”), are in English; pass `label` in your language and translate the units in the copied file.
movimento: Each digit is a wheel that turns by the shortest path, downward each second (00 → 59 is a single step); on first display, the wheels enter in sequence, left to right.
At zero, the digits dissolve with slight scale and blur and give way to `completeLabel`, and the box follows the new width and height with a spring; in `compact`, the pill takes on the success tone.
With “reduce motion”, the digits change without turning, the final swap is a short fade, and the pulsing dot next to the label stays still.
responsivo: In `large`, the digit size follows the container width (`cqi` unit), from 1.75 rem up to display size, and four groups fit in 320 px.
desempenho: The clock only advances while the component is on screen and the tab is visible, and on return it rereads the time, without accumulating delay; a separate timer guarantees the end on time.
notasIA: Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/countdown/countdown`. For a local time, pass `target="2026-12-01T10:00"` and `timeZone="America/Sao_Paulo"`; a string without a time zone and without `timeZone` is read as UTC.
`units` defines what appears, and the largest unit absorbs the rest: with `["hours", "minutes"]`, hours go past 24. If the device clock is not reliable, pass `clock` with the server time.
`onComplete` only fires if the count reaches zero while the component is mounted; if `target` has already passed on mount, it shows `completeLabel` without counting and without calling the callback.
